title: WHY!? YOU'RE CHEATING?!?? | The Sensei Speedrun | GM Naroditsky

moves.spoken: The Queen's Gambit Declined steers the game into positional waters — the gold standard solid answer to 1.d4, never come close to being refuted.
moves.teaches: The QGD is the model solid defense: choose it when you want a positional battle.

moves.spoken: exd5 gives us the Carlsbad structure — a subtly imbalanced formation, named for the city where it appeared in the great early-1900s tournaments, with a lifetime of ideas inside it.
moves.teaches: The QGD exchange leads to the Carlsbad, one of the richest positional structures in chess.

moves.spoken: The first Carlsbad move is c6, reinforcing the d5-pawn that anchors the whole structure.
moves.teaches: Prop up d5 with c6 first; it's the foundation of Black's Carlsbad setup.

moves.spoken: Be7 breaks the pin — the dark bishop's usual square here, though d6 is possible — and h6 can go in any time but isn't obligatory. Then castle, and start the key Carlsbad maneuver: Nbd7 to guard the f6-knight against Bxf6, then Re8 and Nf8, from where the knight both heads to g6 or e6 and defends h7.
moves.teaches: The Carlsbad knight tour is Nbd7-f8-g6/e6; from f8 it also shields h7 against the bishop sac.
